Combining markers with & and | adds one nesting level per operation:

```python
from packaging.markers import Marker
a, b, c = (Marker(f'os_name == "{x}"') for x in "abc")
str((a & b) & c)    # '(os_name == "a" and os_name == "b") and os_name == "c"'

import functools, operator
m = functools.reduce(operator.and_, [Marker(f'os_name == "{i}"') for i in range(2000)])
str(m)              # RecursionError
```

Chaining the same operator must keep the marker flat, so long chains work:
- (a & b) & c prints 'os_name == "a" and os_name == "b" and os_name == "c"'; the same for |;
- a parenthesized group of the same operator is spliced in too: Marker('(os_name == "a" or os_name == "b")') | c prints 'os_name == "a" or os_name == "b" or os_name == "c"';
- a group of the other operator keeps its parentheses: with ab = Marker('os_name == "a" or os_name == "b"'), str(ab & c & c) is '(os_name == "a" or os_name == "b") and os_name == "c" and os_name == "c"', and str(c | (c & c)) is 'os_name == "c" or (os_name == "c" and os_name == "c")';
- a chain of 2000 markers built with & or | prints without parentheses, and survives Marker(str(m)) == m and a pickle round trip.
